speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you've had a tympanoplasty and are experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings; can you describe exactly where the pain is located and if it radiates anywhere?

Did you notice any drainage, fever, or change in hearing since your surgery?

Are you currently taking any pain medication or antibiotics, and if so, how effective have they been?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Incus dislocation (Tympanosclerosis) or Ossicular chain disruption. The patient's history of chronic ear infections and the specific complaint of "shooting pain when eating" (jaw movement) combined with "difficulty wearing earrings" (pain on manipulation) strongly suggests an anatomical issue with the ossicular chain, likely caused by scarring (tympanosclerosis) or a fracture/dislocation that occurred during the healing phase of the tympanoplasty. The improved hearing on the audiology report may be misleading if it did not include bone conduction testing or if the report was from before the new symptoms fully manifested. I will request images to confirm the integrity of the ossicles. REQUEST IMAGES: Temporal_Bone_CT_with_Ossicular_Imaging.
